title: Ch-N-N
hook: chen, grace; chanun, gracious, in the thirteen attributes

segments.voice: Yesterday, R-Ch-M: rechem and rachamim, the womb and mercy, and a mother at Solomon's court. Your line was mercy is womb-love. Who got a parent's answer from you? Today, the word that stands right next to mercy on the mountain. Day one thousand three hundred eighty-one.

The first tablets lie broken at the foot of the mountain, smashed after the golden calf. Moses makes a bold request. In the King James: "I beseech thee, shew me thy glory." The answer is no, and yes. No face. But God will pass by while Moses stands hidden in a cleft of the rock, and God will call out names. So Moses climbs again, carrying two new stone tablets. When it happens, he doesn't see a shape. He hears a list. And right beside mercy in that list stands today's root.
screen: `SHEW ME THY GLORY.` → `TWO NEW TABLETS.` → `NOT A FACE: A LIST OF NAMES.`

segments.voice: Ch-N-N. Chet, nun, nun. Chen, grace, favor. Chanun, gracious. Turn it four ways. First, an earlier verse. When the flood story opens, the world has gone bad, and then comes a short line: "But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD." Grace there is chen. Notice the order. The verse doesn't give a reason first; only after it does the text call Noah a just man. Some readers hear that as the shape of grace: favor that arrives before anyone earns it. Second, back on the mountain. God passes by and proclaims, in the King James: "The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth." Merciful is rachum, from yesterday's root. Gracious is chanun, from today's. The two stand side by side, as if one needs the other. Third, the priestly blessing from a few days ago, one line further on: "The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee." The same root, in the middle of the blessing, asked for every time it's said. Fourth, the list said aloud. Tradition counts the qualities Moses heard as thirteen attributes, and congregations chant them together on fast days and in the season of the High Holy Days. A people asking to be forgiven reaches for the words God used just after the golden calf. So grace in this root isn't a reward. It's the extra that's given when nothing is owed.
screen: `NOAH FOUND GRACE.` · `MERCIFUL AND GRACIOUS.` · `BE GRACIOUS UNTO THEE.` · `THE ATTRIBUTES, SAID ALOUD.` · then, large: `חֵן · חַנּוּן`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan one gracious act. Settle, and breathe. Grace, in this root, is giving more than is owed. Look ahead at the rest of your day. Where will someone be owed exactly nothing from you? The driver trying to merge. The cashier who's slow. The person who interrupts. The one who apologized badly. Pick one moment and decide, now, to give a little more than the rule requires: room, patience, a real thank-you, a pass. See it happen. If you pray, you can ask, in the words of the blessing, that God be gracious to you, and to them. The bell holds the time.
Ch-N-N. Chet, nun, nun: chen, grace, the favor Noah found, and chanun, gracious, standing beside merciful in the attributes. Today's word.
Your line: grace. Today, when that moment comes, give the extra nobody asked for, and don't mention it. Day one thousand three hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Jews chant the thirteen attributes of mercy, drawn from Exodus 34:6–7, aloud on fast days and during the High Holy Days, and the priestly blessing asks that God 'be gracious unto thee'.

notes: Quotations from the KJV; confirm the Judaism path accepts KJV here.
'The second quality in that list' (hook): in Exodus 34:6 after the divine name(s), rachum is first and chanun second. Confirm this framing, or cut 'second'.
The count 'thirteen attributes' is given as tradition's count, per the index; Exodus 34:6–7 itself does not number them.
Chanting the attributes 'on fast days and through the High Holy Days' describes common liturgical practice (Selichot, Yom Kippur); confirm, or soften.
'Some readers hear that as the shape of grace' (Genesis 6:8 before 6:9) is framed as a reading.

Editor: hook reordered to match Exodus 33:18 to 34:4 (the request for glory comes before the new tablets); cut invented 'one request left' and the ambiguous 'second quality'; priestly blessing marked as a callback to day 1375; 'Jews chant' softened to 'congregations chant'; repeated 'after the calf' ending trimmed.
